newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges down to 10.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges down to 10.2 pct.

text.p: Croatian average lending rate edged down to 10.2 percent from 11.2 percent on Tuesday in dwindling trade amid shrinking demand for kuna funds.
Total daily trade was put at modest 13 million kuna against the supply of 45 million.
Interbank rates ranged from 9.0 percent for call money borrowings and insurers' loans to 16 percent for long-term funds, delears said.
Overnight trade was put at 93.6 million kuna, of which only 3.6 million were used by a bank with shortfalls. Other banks sought funds to keep their mandatory reserve requirements.
The central bank's exchange rates for Wednesday eased to 5.4326 versus the dollar and to 3.5661 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
